title: Research apprenticeship and qualifying exams
stage: Graduate study and research in machine learning
audience: a graduate preparing for research in machine learning, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Complete the first milestones of a research career in machine learning: reproduce a published result and extend it, write it up as a workshop paper and present it, prepare for qualifying exams that span theory, methods and applications, and choose a thesis direction and plan the next steps toward a PhD or a research role.
primary_reading: OpenReview: public peer reviews of machine learning papers (free)

weeks.2: Planning a reproduction: scope, compute and success criteria
weeks.4: When results do not match: debugging and honest reporting
weeks.5: Extending a result: ablations and new settings
weeks.7: Qualifying exam review: theory and optimization
weeks.8: Qualifying exam review: models and methods
weeks.9: Qualifying exam review: applications and responsible AI
weeks.11: Choosing a thesis direction and an advisor
weeks.12: Paths in research: PhD programs, industry labs and independent research

blocks.deliverable: Report your first results with their uncertainty.
Draft the paper's method and results sections.
Week 7 midterm; answer timed questions on theory and methods.
Take a mock oral exam on your reading list.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Reproduction paper: reproduce one result from a published machine learning paper with modest compute, extend it with one ablation or new setting, write a four- to six-page workshop-style paper that reports honestly what did and did not reproduce, release your code with instructions, and pass a mock qualifying exam of three timed answers.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
